newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Top Colombian cop wants drug suspect sent to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Top Colombian cop wants drug suspect sent to U.S..

text.p: Colombia's police chief said on Monday he would prefer a top Colombian drug suspect held in Venezuela to be extradited to the United States rather than to Colombia.
Justo Pastor Perafan, believed to be the last Colombian drug billionaire not in jail or dead, was arrested last Friday in the western town of San Cristobal, across the border from Colombia.

"In my opinion, it would be better to take him to the United States because in Colombia the only charge against him is one of illicit enrichment," Colombian police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano told Union Radio.

Perafan, who is being held at military intelligence headquarters in Caracas, is wanted on drug charges in New York. Colombian police said there were eight charges pending against him for introducing five cocaine shipments between 1988 and 1994.

The U.S. ambassador to Venezuela, John Maisto, has filed a petition for Perafan's detention, the first step towards an extradition request. Colombia has asked Venezuela to deport or extradite Perafan. The Supreme Court will decide.

Serrano, explaining why he would rather see Perafan put on trial in the United States, said of Colombia's judicial system: "One gets disillusioned because so many juridical complications...allow these people to quickly walk free again."

Colombia's constitution forbids extradition of its citizens from its soil. President Ernesto Samper this month called for an end to this ban, but the move must be approved by Congress and this is likely to take months.

Perafan, who was using an alias and had undergone plastic surgery and hair implants to change his appearance, was described as among the wealthiest drug lords still on the run with a personal fortune estimated at $12 billion.
